newsitem.title: CANADA: Eggleton says Chile trade deal still not final.
newsitem.headline: Eggleton says Chile trade deal still not final.

text.p: Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton on Thursday said a free trade agreement between Canada and Chile was still not finalized, as a result of last-minute "hiccups" in the negotiations.

"There has been a last-minute hiccup. There still is a review that is going on in Santiago, and as a result of that this matter is not yet finalized," Eggleton told reporters at a press conference, minutes after the International Trade Department released a statement declaring that a final agreement had been reached.

"There are very few items that are still a part of consideration on the Chile side... They've asked for further discussion on a couple of product items," Eggleton said, adding that the last-minute delay had come very much as a surprise.
He said he could not discuss any details until the agreement was finalized.

The free trade agreement between Ottawa and Santiago was supposed to be signed during a visit by Chilean President Eduardo Frei to Canada this weekend. There were no details on whether the visit would still take place as scheduled.
A planned visit by Frei to Ottawa in September was cancelled because a free trade agreement could not be reached in time.
Eggleton said he hoped that the last-minute dispute would be resolved "very soon."

"I'm hopeful that that is going to be resolved in a matter of hours," he said, noting that the press release issued by his department had been cancelled and would not be valid until the deal is finalized.
Eggleton said he did not expect this to happen by the end of Thursday, but possibly on Friday. He said he did not think there was any chance that the deal would fall through.
"I don't think that that's going to happen. Not for a minute," Eggleton said.
He said the problems under discussion were "specific product items", not the basic principles of the arrangement.
A member of Canada's negotiating team, which returned to Ottawa late Wednesday, said an agreement had been reached late that day. The latest problems arose after the Canadian team had left Santiago.
The free trade deal between Canada and Chile is widely seen as a stepping stone for Chile to join the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which groups Canada, the United States and Mexico.
Some of the provisions of the agreement between Ottawa and Santiago were modelled on similar NAFTA clauses.
Eggleton said the United States had shown an active interest in the negotiations between Ottawa and Santiago.
"They have been quite interested in this arrangement between Canada and Chile as it has been negotiated to this point," he said.

"I suspect the (Clinton) administration will want to get to the table soon, but they'll have to of course deal with the Congress on this matter, and meanwhile we'll have a bilateral agreement once we get these final matters finalized between Canada and Chile," Eggleton said.
